name: Non-text Content
summary: Every piece of non-text content shown to users has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose. Controls and inputs need a name that describes their purpose. Time-based media, tests that would be invalid in text, and content meant to create a specific sensory experience only need a text alternative that identifies them. A CAPTCHA needs a text alternative describing its purpose and a version that uses a different sense. Content that is pure decoration, used only for visual formatting, or not presented to users must be implemented so assistive technology can ignore it.
whyItMatters: Alt text can be present and equivalent yet still tiring to use, for example when it repeats the caption beside it or runs to a paragraph.

provisions.title: Image Alternatives Available
provisions.text: Text alternatives are available for non-decorative images.

provisions.title: Image Alternatives Equivalent
provisions.text: Text alternatives for non-decorative images convey the equivalent purpose to the image.

provisions.title: Decorative Images Hidden
provisions.text: Decorative images are programmatically hidden.

provisions.title: Non-text content not relied on
provisions.text: All non-text content that is not decorative includes a programmatically determinable equivalent text alternative.

related.title: Images Detectable
related.text: Non-decorative images are detectable.

name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded audio-only content has a text alternative that presents equivalent information (an "alternative for time-based media"). Prerecorded video-only content has either that text alternative or an audio track with equivalent information. Media that is itself an alternative for text, and clearly labeled as such, is exempt.
whyItMatters: A transcript that technically exists but sits on another page, or is only linked from a footer, is easy to miss. Users who need it may never find it.

provisions.title: Descriptive Transcripts Available
provisions.text: Descriptive transcripts are provided for prerecorded audio and video content.
exceptWhen:
• The media is purely decorative.
  • The media is already a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
  • The visual track includes no information that is not already conveyed in the audio track (for example, a “talking head” video where only the speaker is visible against a static background).

provisions.title: Dialogue transcripts available (prerecorded)
provisions.text: Dialogue transcripts are available for all prerecorded audio and video content.
exceptWhen:
• The audio or video content is an alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
  • The audio or video has no spoken content and serves only as background.

provisions.title: Transcripts equivalent (prerecorded)
provisions.text: Equivalent transcripts are available for audio and video content.
exceptWhen: • The audio or video has no spoken content and serves only as background.

name: Captions (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded audio in synchronized media (video with sound) has captions. By definition, captions cover both speech and the non-speech audio needed to understand the content. Media that is a clearly labeled alternative for text is exempt.
whyItMatters: Complete captions can still be hard to follow when they are split mid-phrase, cover on-screen text, or can't be resized.

provisions.title: Captions available (prerecorded)
provisions.text: Captions are available for all prerecorded audio content.
exceptWhen: • The audio content is an alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.

provisions.title: Captions equivalent (prerecorded)
provisions.text: Equivalent captions are available for audio and video content.
exceptWhen: • The audio or video has no spoken content and serves only as background.

provisions.title: Captions Synchronized
provisions.text: Captions are synchronized with the audio content of synchronized media.

provisions.title: Sounds Identified In Captions
provisions.text: Sounds needed to understand the media are identified or described in captions.
exceptWhen: • the video is decorative.

related.title: Speakers Identified In Captions
related.text: Speakers are identified understandably within all captions.
exceptWhen:
• The speaker has a hidden identity as part of narrative structure.
  • Identity is identifiable within the context of use.

name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded video with sound has either a full text alternative for time-based media or audio description of the video. Media that is a clearly labeled alternative for text is exempt.
whyItMatters: Meeting Level A with a text document means blind users leave the video to read instead of experiencing it with everyone else.

provisions.title: Audio descriptions available (prerecorded)
provisions.text: Audio descriptions are available in prerecorded video for visual content needed to understand the media.
exceptWhen: the video content is an alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.

provisions.title: Descriptive Transcripts Available
provisions.text: Descriptive transcripts are provided for prerecorded audio and video content.
exceptWhen:
• The media is purely decorative.
  • The media is already a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
  • The visual track includes no information that is not already conveyed in the audio track (for example, a “talking head” video where only the speaker is visible against a static background).

name: Captions (Live)
summary: Live audio in synchronized media, such as a live-streamed event with video, has captions.
whyItMatters: Complete live captions that lag well behind the speaker are hard to follow alongside the video.

provisions.title: Captions available (live)
provisions.text: Captions are available for all live audio content.

name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded video in synchronized media has audio description: narration added to describe important visual details that can't be understood from the main soundtrack alone.
whyItMatters: Description squeezed into short pauses can leave out context. A separate described version is often hard to find, or lags behind updates to the main video.

provisions.title: Audio descriptions available (prerecorded)
provisions.text: Audio descriptions are available in prerecorded video for visual content needed to understand the media.
exceptWhen: the video content is an alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.

provisions.title: Audio descriptions equivalent (prerecorded)
provisions.text: The information conveyed by audio descriptions is equivalent to the visual content needed to understand the media.

provisions.title: Audio Descriptions Synchronized
provisions.text: Audio descriptions are synchronized with video content without overlapping dialogue and meaningful audio content.
exceptWhen: • There are no audio descriptions.

provisions.title: Visual Information Identified In Audio Descriptions
provisions.text: Visual information needed to understand the media is described in audio descriptions.

name: Info and Relationships
summary: Information, structure and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined, or are available in text. If something looks like a heading, list, table or group, that structure has to be available to software too.
whyItMatters: A page can convey its structure with the bare minimum of semantics and still be slow to navigate. Without landmarks or a sensible heading outline, screen reader users have fewer ways to jump around.

provisions.title: Relationships Detectable
provisions.text: Relationships of meaning between elements are conveyed programmatically.

provisions.title: Heading Structure Available
provisions.text: Meaningful blocks of content are organized with a logical hierarchy of headings.
exceptWhen: • The technology does not support heading levels.

provisions.title: Blocks of content available (minimum)
provisions.text: Meaningful blocks of content are programmatically determinable and visually presented with sufficient surrounding space.

provisions.title: Order Detectable
provisions.text: Ordered content includes programmatically determinable markers that indicate the position of each item.
exceptWhen: • The nature of the ordering of the content is presented immediately prior.

provisions.title: Sections Labeled
provisions.text: Meaningful blocks of content have a semantically appropriate label that defines their purpose.
exceptWhen: • A label is not needed to understand the purpose of the content within the context of use.

related.title: Text Appearance Not Relied On
related.text: Meaning conveyed by text style properties is also programmatically determinable.
exceptWhen: • emphasis is the only additional meaning conveyed.

name: Meaningful Sequence
summary: When the order of content affects its meaning, a correct reading order can be programmatically determined.
whyItMatters: CSS that reorders content visually (flex order, grid placement) can still pass, yet keyboard and screen magnifier users see focus and reading jump around the screen.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft addresses reading sequence.

name: Sensory Characteristics
summary: Instructions for understanding and operating content don't rely solely on sensory characteristics such as shape, color, size, visual location, orientation or sound.
whyItMatters: Instructions that lead with position ("in the panel on the right") still slow down people who can't see the layout, or who see a reflowed version of it.

provisions.title: Sensory Characteristics Not Relied On
provisions.text: Instructions and help do not rely on sensory characteristics.

name: Orientation
summary: Content doesn't restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation (portrait or landscape) unless a specific orientation is essential.
whyItMatters: Content that technically rotates can still be awkward. In landscape on a phone, fixed headers and footers can leave only a sliver of usable space.

provisions.title: Orientation supported (minimum)
provisions.text: If the platform has a default orientation, content supports that orientation. If the platform does not have a default orientation, content supports both portrait and landscape orientations.
exceptWhen:
• Content is aligned with the physical world.
  • The orientation is essential.

provisions.title: Orientation supported (enhanced)
provisions.text: Content supports both portrait and landscape orientations.
exceptWhen:
• Content is aligned with the physical world.
  • The orientation is essential.

name: Identify Input Purpose
summary: Input fields collecting information about the user have a programmatically determinable purpose, when the field's purpose is one listed in WCAG's Input Purposes section and the technology supports it. (In HTML, W3C's sufficient technique is the autocomplete attribute; techniques are informative.)
whyItMatters: Correct autocomplete values don't help if scripts or browser workarounds stop autofill from working. People with motor or memory impairments are left retyping their details.

related.title: Automated Entry Allowed
related.text: Automated input of personal information from user agents, third-party tools, or paste is not prevented.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft requires identifying input purpose. Automated entry allowed covers not blocking autofill or paste.

name: Use of Color
summary: Color is not the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
whyItMatters: A second cue that meets 3:1 but is small, such as a small icon beside a red error message, is still easy for color-blind users to miss.

provisions.title: Hue Not Relied On
provisions.text: Information is not conveyed by hue alone.
exceptWhen:
• Content is artistic or expressive.
  • Content is designed only for a device that is limited to presenting hues.

name: Audio Control
summary: If audio plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, there is either a way to pause or stop it, or a way to control its volume separately from the system volume. Under WCAG's non-interference requirement this applies to everything on the page, even content not relied on to meet other criteria.
whyItMatters: A pause button at the bottom of the page is hard to find for screen reader users, whose speech is drowned out by the audio while they look for it.

provisions.title: Page/view audio adjustable
provisions.text: A mechanism is available to pause, stop, and adjust the volume independently of the overall system volume level, of any automatically playing audio in a page/view.

name: Contrast (Minimum)
summary: Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1. Large-scale text (at least 18pt, or 14pt bold) needs 3:1. Text in inactive components, pure decoration, invisible text, text inside pictures with significant other visual content, and logos have no contrast requirement.
whyItMatters: 4.5:1 is a floor. Thin or small fonts at exactly 4.5:1 can still be hard to read for people with low vision, in glare, or on low-quality screens.

provisions.title: Text contrast sufficient (minimum)
provisions.text: The default visual presentation of text meets @@[contrast measure to be determined].
exceptWhen:
• the text is:
    • also present elsewhere in the page/view which meets the requirement
    • part of an inactive interactive element
    • pure decoration
    • not visible to anyone
    • part of a picture that includes significant other visual content
    • part of a logo or brand name

changeAnalysis.note: The draft's contrast measure is still to be determined.

name: Resize Text
summary: Apart from captions and images of text, text can be resized up to 200 percent without assistive technology and without loss of content or functionality.
whyItMatters: Many people enlarge only the text, through browser or OS font settings rather than zoom. Layouts with fixed heights can clip that text even when they pass with page zoom.

provisions.title: Text Size Adjustable
provisions.text: Text can be increased in size to at least 200% of the platform’s default body-text size.
exceptWhen: • the same text is available elsewhere in the page/view which can be increased to at least 200% of the platform’s default body-text size.

name: Images of Text
summary: If the technology can produce the visual presentation, real text is used instead of images of text. Exceptions: the image of text can be visually customized (font, size, color and background can be set), or a particular presentation is essential.
whyItMatters: Text baked into banners and social cards can't be resized, recolored or reflowed, and blurs when magnified.

related.title: Text Detectable
related.text: All visible text has a programmatically determinable equivalent.
exceptWhen: • making visible text programmatically determinable would lead to duplication within the view.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft restricts images of text.

name: Reflow
summary: Content can be presented without losing information or functionality, and without scrolling in two directions, at a width of 320 CSS pixels (for vertically scrolling content) or a height of 256 CSS pixels (for horizontally scrolling content). Parts of the content that need a two-dimensional layout for their use or meaning are exempt.
whyItMatters: A page can reflow while hiding key actions behind menus, or by covering much of the small viewport with sticky headers. People using 400% zoom then see very little content at once.

provisions.title: Layout Reflow Supported
provisions.text: All content fits within 320 CSS pixels in the default orientation of text without requiring scrolling in more than one direction. Sections of content within the page/view that scroll in a different direction to the page/view fit within 320 CSS pixels of the page-scrolling direction.
exceptWhen:
• 2D relationships (for example, tables or electronic program guides)
  • canvases of presentational content (for example, slides)
  • multiple palettes or panels that act on content (for example, Photoshop or an IDE)

provisions.title: Text Reflow Supported
provisions.text: Blocks of text are legible at 320 CSS pixels in the orientation of text, without the need to scroll in the orientation of text.
exceptWhen: • The meaning of text relies on a two-dimensional structure.

name: Non-text Contrast
summary: These have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors: the visual information needed to identify user interface components and their states (except inactive components, and components whose appearance is set by the browser and not modified by the author), and the parts of graphics needed to understand the content (unless a particular presentation is essential).
whyItMatters: A state change that meets 3:1 but is shown only by a thin border change is easy to miss.

provisions.title: Interactive Element Contrast Sufficient
provisions.text: Visual information required to identify interactive elements and states meet a minimum contrast ratio test.
exceptWhen:
• The interactive element is inactive, or
  • The appearance of the component is determined by the user agent and not modified by the content author.

provisions.title: Graphical Object Contrast Sufficient
provisions.text: Parts of graphical objects required to understand the content meet a minimum contrast ratio test
exceptWhen: • a particular presentation of graphical objects is essential to the information being conveyed.

name: Text Spacing
summary: In content built with markup languages, nothing is lost and nothing stops working when a user sets line height to 1.5 times the font size, spacing after paragraphs to 2 times, letter spacing to 0.12 times and word spacing to 0.16 times, changing no other style. Languages and scripts that don't use one of these properties are exempt for that property.
whyItMatters: Layouts can survive the test values exactly but break with slightly larger user settings, or with fonts swapped in for dyslexia.

provisions.title: Text Style Adjustable
provisions.text: The presentation of text style properties can be adjusted, without loss of content or functionality, to meet the @@ [values to be determined] for: * typeface * font width * text decoration * capitalization * automatic end-of-line hyphenation
exceptWhen: • the text style property is hard-coded, such as raw text that is capitalized or hyphenated.

provisions.title: Blocks Of Text Adjustable
provisions.text: The presentation of blocks of text can be adjusted, without loss of content or functionality, to meet the @@ [values to be determined] for: * inline margin * block margin * line length * line height * justification
exceptWhen: • the style attribute is hard-coded, such as raw text that is capitalized or hyphenated.

name: Content on Hover or Focus
summary: When hover or keyboard focus makes extra content appear (such as a custom tooltip or submenu): it can be dismissed without moving the pointer or focus, unless it shows an input error or doesn't cover other content; if triggered by hover, the pointer can move onto it without it disappearing; and it stays visible until the trigger is removed, the user dismisses it, or its information is no longer valid. Content whose presentation the browser controls, such as a title-attribute tooltip, is exempt.
whyItMatters: Hover content can pass and still be awkward on touch screens, where there is no hover, and for magnifier users who lose it off-screen.

provisions.title: Hover Or Focus Content Dismissible
provisions.text: A mechanism is available to dismiss content that appears on pointer hover or keyboard focus without moving pointer hover or keyboard focus, unless the additional content does not obscure or replace other content.

provisions.title: Hover Content Persistent
provisions.text: If pointer hover can trigger content, then the pointer can be moved over the additional content without the additional content disappearing.

provisions.title: Hover Or Focus Content Persistent
provisions.text: Content that appears on pointer hover or keyboard focus remains visible until the hover or keyboard focus trigger is removed, the user dismisses it, or its information is no longer valid.

name: Keyboard
summary: All functionality can be operated through a keyboard interface, without needing specific timing for individual keystrokes. The exception is functionality whose underlying function depends on the path of the user's movement, not just its endpoints (such as freehand drawing).
whyItMatters: Something can be keyboard-operable yet take dozens of Tab presses, or rely on key combinations nobody would guess.

provisions.title: Keyboard Operable
provisions.text: All components on the page/view that can be operated by pointer, audio (voice or other), gesture, camera, or other means can be operated using keyboard interface only.

provisions.title: Keyboard Accessible
provisions.text: All content that can be accessed by other input modalities can be accessed using keyboard interface only.

name: No Keyboard Trap
summary: If keyboard focus can move into a component, it can move out again using only the keyboard. If leaving needs more than unmodified arrow or Tab keys or another standard exit method, the user is told how. Under WCAG's non-interference requirement this applies to everything on the page.
whyItMatters: A non-standard exit that is documented somewhere technically passes, but users rarely find the instructions.

provisions.title: No Keyboard Traps
provisions.text: Components that can be activated or entered using the keyboard interface, can be deactivated or exited using a standard keyboard navigation-operation technique, standard platform keyboard commands.
exceptWhen: • The non-standard keyboard navigation technique is described in the page/view or earlier in the process.

name: Character Key Shortcuts
summary: If a keyboard shortcut uses only a letter, punctuation, number or symbol key, at least one of these is true: it can be turned off; it can be remapped to include a non-printable key such as Ctrl or Alt; or it only works while the relevant component has focus.
whyItMatters: A setting to turn shortcuts off that is hard to find leaves speech-input users accidentally triggering actions until they discover it.

provisions.title: No Keyboard Conflicts
provisions.text: Custom keyboard commands do not conflict with standard platform keyboard commands or they can be remapped.

name: Timing Adjustable
summary: For each time limit the content sets, at least one is true: the user can turn it off before reaching it; adjust it to at least ten times the default; or is warned before it expires and given at least 20 seconds to extend it with a simple action, at least ten times. The limit is exempt if it's a required part of a real-time event with no possible alternative, if it's essential and extending it would invalidate the activity, or if it's longer than 20 hours.
whyItMatters: Twenty seconds to respond to a warning is short for people using screen readers, switch access or speech input, especially if the warning doesn't take focus or isn't announced.

provisions.title: Timeout Adjustable
provisions.text: A mechanism exists to extend the time limit before timeout, or the time limit can be disabled.
exceptWhen: • The time limit is essential.

provisions.title: Time Limits Conveyed
provisions.text: Users are informed at the start of the process or session that a time limit exists, its length, and that it can be adjusted.
exceptWhen: • hiding the existence of the time limit is essential.

name: Pause, Stop, Hide
summary: Moving, blinking or scrolling information that starts automatically, lasts more than five seconds and is shown alongside other content can be paused, stopped or hidden, unless the movement is essential. Auto-updating information that starts automatically and is shown alongside other content can be paused, stopped or hidden, or its update frequency controlled, unless essential. Under WCAG's non-interference requirement this applies to everything on the page.
whyItMatters: A small pause button that is hard to find, or that resets when the page reloads, still passes. Motion can distract people with attention-related disabilities long before they find it.

provisions.title: No Visual Motion
provisions.text: Content does not include pseudo-motion or visual motion lasting longer than 5 seconds.
exceptWhen: • The motion or pseudo-motion is essential.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers auto-updating content.

name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
summary: Nothing on the page flashes more than three times in any one second, or the flashing is below the general flash and red flash thresholds defined in WCAG. Under WCAG's non-interference requirement this applies to everything on the page.
whyItMatters: The thresholds are approximations. Content near them can still affect some people with photosensitive epilepsy, or cause migraines.

provisions.title: No Flashing Over Threshold
provisions.text: Flashes are below the general flash and red flash thresholds.
exceptWhen: • The flashing is essential.

name: Bypass Blocks
summary: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple pages.
whyItMatters: Headings and landmarks help screen reader users but do nothing for sighted keyboard users, who must still tab through the whole header.

provisions.title: Focus Relevant
provisions.text: The focus order does not include hidden, static, or groups of repeated interactive elements.

changeAnalysis.note: Focus relevant's test procedure asks for a way to skip groups of repeated interactive elements, such as site navigation.

name: Page Titled
summary: Pages have titles that describe their topic or purpose.
whyItMatters: Descriptive titles with the site name first get cut off in narrow browser tabs, so users can't tell tabs apart.

provisions.title: Page/view title available
provisions.text: The page/view has a title that describes its name, topic, or purpose.
exceptWhen: • The technology has no way to include a title.

name: Focus Order
summary: If a page can be navigated sequentially and the order affects meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
whyItMatters: An order that preserves meaning can still jump around the screen, which disorients sighted keyboard and magnifier users.

provisions.title: Focus Order Meaningful
provisions.text: The keyboard focus moves sequentially through content in an order and way that preserves meaning and operability.

name: Link Purpose (In Context)
summary: The purpose of each link can be determined from its text alone, or from its text together with its programmatically determined context, except where the purpose would be ambiguous to everyone.
whyItMatters: Screen reader users who browse a list of links hear "Read more" ten times with no context, even though each link passes.

related.title: Interactive Element Names Available
related.text: Persistent names (including labels) that identify the purpose of the interactive element are visually and programmatically available.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers link purpose.

name: Headings and Labels
summary: The headings and labels you provide describe their topic or purpose.
whyItMatters: Headings that are accurate but vague ("Details", "More") pass, yet make scanning slow.

provisions.title: Sections Labeled
provisions.text: Meaningful blocks of content have a semantically appropriate label that defines their purpose.
exceptWhen: • A label is not needed to understand the purpose of the content within the context of use.

related.title: Interactive Element Names Available
related.text: Persistent names (including labels) that identify the purpose of the interactive element are visually and programmatically available.

name: Focus Visible
summary: Any keyboard-operable interface has a mode of operation in which the keyboard focus indicator is visible.
whyItMatters: A visible indicator, even one that meets 3:1, can be hard to spot if it's thin or close in style to the hover state.

related.title: Focus Indicator Contrast Sufficient
related.text: If a custom focus indicator is used, it has sufficient adjacent contrast and change of contrast.

related.title: Default Focus Indicator Used
related.text: The focusable item uses the user agent default focus indicator.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft requires a visible focus indicator as such; the related provisions cover its contrast and the use of the browser default.

name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
summary: When a component receives keyboard focus, it is not entirely hidden by content the author created.
whyItMatters: A focused field that is 90% hidden behind a sticky footer passes, but keyboard users can't see what they're typing into.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers focus being obscured.

name: Label in Name
summary: For components whose label includes text or images of text, the accessible name contains the text that is shown visually.
whyItMatters: If the visible words sit in the middle of a longer name, some speech-input tools match less reliably.

provisions.title: Label Included In Programmatic Name
provisions.text: The programmatic name includes the visual label.

name: Dragging Movements
summary: Functionality that uses dragging can also be done with a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential or the browser provides the functionality and the author hasn't modified it.
whyItMatters: An alternative that takes many taps, or sits in an overflow menu, technically passes but is tiring for people with motor impairments.

provisions.title: Simple Pointer Input Available
provisions.text: All functionality and content available using complex pointer inputs is also available using a simple pointer input, or a sequence of simple pointer inputs that do not require timing.

name: Target Size (Minimum)
summary: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except when: a 24 CSS pixel circle centered on each smaller target doesn't overlap another target or another such circle; the same function is available through another control on the page that meets this criterion; the target is in a sentence or limited by the line height of surrounding text; the browser sets the size and the author hasn't changed it; or the presentation is essential or legally required.
whyItMatters: 24 by 24 is still small for people with tremors or limited dexterity. Targets that pass only through spacing are easy to miss.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers target size.

name: Language of Page
summary: The default human language of each page can be programmatically determined. (In HTML, W3C's sufficient technique is the lang attribute on the html element; techniques are informative.)
whyItMatters: A correct but generic code, such as en with no region, can't tell a screen reader which accent or spelling conventions to use.

provisions.title: Human Language Detectable
provisions.text: The human language of all content within the view is programmatically determinable.
exceptWhen:
• A language tag is not available in [[iso-639-2023]], or
  • The technology used to create the view does not support indicating languages.

name: Language of Parts
summary: The human language of each passage or phrase can be programmatically determined. Exempt: proper names, technical terms, words of indeterminate language, and words or phrases that have become part of the surrounding language.
whyItMatters: Proper names and technical terms are exempt, so a page full of untagged foreign names can still be mispronounced.

provisions.title: Human Language Detectable
provisions.text: The human language of all content within the view is programmatically determinable.
exceptWhen:
• A language tag is not available in [[iso-639-2023]], or
  • The technology used to create the view does not support indicating languages.

name: On Focus
summary: When any component receives focus, that doesn't start a change of context. WCAG defines a change of context as a change of user agent, viewport, focus, or content that changes the meaning of the page.
whyItMatters: Focus-triggered changes that fall short of a "change of context", such as large panels expanding, can still disorient people using magnification.

related.title: Change Of Focus Notified
related.text: When the focus changes on-focus or automatically, the user is notified visually and programmatically.

related.title: Focus user-controlled
related.text: The keyboard focus only moves as a result of user interaction.
exceptWhen:
• The keyboard focus automatically moves to the next interactive elements in keyboard navigation order on completion of some user action, such when the focus moves between the fields for a time-based one-time password (TOTP) code.
  • The keyboard focus results from security or emergency situations, such as warning about an imminent session timeout that would cause the user to lose their work.
  • The user is informed of the potential keyboard focus move before it happens and given the chance to avoid the move.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft forbids a change of context on focus; the related ones cover notification and focus movement.

name: On Input
summary: Changing the setting of a component doesn't automatically cause a change of context, unless the user was told about this behavior before using the component.
whyItMatters: Advance notice that is technically present, such as a sentence above the form, is easily missed. Keyboard users browsing a select with arrow keys can trigger navigation by accident.

related.title: Change Of User Agent Notified
related.text: When content triggers a device change or an automatic user agent change, the user is notified before the change occurs.

related.title: Page/view change notified
related.text: When content triggers a change of page/view there is a visual change within the view and programmatic notification of the change.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft forbids a change of context on input.

name: Consistent Help
summary: If pages in a set repeat any of these help mechanisms, they appear in the same order relative to other page content, unless the user changes it: human contact details, a human contact mechanism, a self-help option, or a fully automated contact mechanism.
whyItMatters: Consistently placed help can still be unhelpful, such as a chatbot that can't reach a person.

provisions.title: Consistent Help Available
provisions.text: Help is labeled consistently and is available in a consistent location relative to other content.

name: Error Identification
summary: If an input error is automatically detected, the item in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
whyItMatters: An error summary that names fields but is not linked to them makes screen reader users hunt back through the form to find each problem.

provisions.title: Error Notifications Available
provisions.text: Errors that are programmatically determined are identified and the problem is described to the user in text.

provisions.title: Errors Associated
provisions.text: When input validation fails, the errors are visually and programmatically associated with the element that caused the error or that can resolve it.

name: Labels or Instructions
summary: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input. WCAG defines a label as text, or a component with a text alternative, presented to the user to identify a component.
whyItMatters: Placeholder-only labels disappear as soon as people type, so users with memory or attention difficulties lose track of what a field wants, and prefilled fields can't be checked.

provisions.title: Interactive Element Names Available
provisions.text: Persistent names (including labels) that identify the purpose of the interactive element are visually and programmatically available.

provisions.title: Input Constraints Used
provisions.text: Field constraints and conditions are available.

related.title: Process Instructions Available
related.text: The instructions needed to complete a multi-step process are available.

name: Redundant Entry
summary: Information the user has already entered, or that was provided to them, and that must be entered again in the same process, is either auto-populated or available to select. Exceptions: re-entry is essential, is needed for security, or the earlier information is no longer valid.
whyItMatters: Offering the earlier value in a hard-to-find control satisfies "available to select" but still makes people re-enter data.

provisions.title: No Redundant Entry
provisions.text: Information previously entered by or provided to the user that is required to be entered again in the same process is either auto-populated, or available for the user to select.
exceptWhen:
• Re-entering the information is essential,
  • The information is required to ensure the security of the content, or
  • Previously entered information is no longer valid.

name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
summary: No step of an authentication process requires a cognitive function test, unless that step offers one of: another method that doesn't rely on one; a mechanism to help complete it; a test that is recognizing objects; or a test that is identifying non-text content the user provided. WCAG defines a cognitive function test as remembering, manipulating or transcribing information, such as remembering a password, transcribing characters, correct spelling, calculations or puzzles. Name, email and phone number don't count.
whyItMatters: Object-recognition CAPTCHAs are allowed at AA but are still very hard for many blind and low-vision users and people with cognitive disabilities.

provisions.title: Cognitive Test Alternatives Available
provisions.text: Processes can be completed without a cognitive function test.

provisions.title: Automated Entry Allowed
provisions.text: Automated input of personal information from user agents, third-party tools, or paste is not prevented.

related.title: Biometrics Not Relied On
related.text: Biometric identification is not the only way to identify or authenticate.

name: Name, Role, Value
summary: For all interface components (including form elements, links and scripted components), the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties and values the user can set can be programmatically set; and changes to them are notified to user agents, including assistive technologies.
whyItMatters: Custom widgets can expose a valid name and role yet not match expected keyboard behavior or announce in a useful order.

provisions.title: Roles, values, states, properties available
provisions.text: Accurate names, roles, values, and states are available for interactive elements.

provisions.title: Interactive Element Names Available
provisions.text: Persistent names (including labels) that identify the purpose of the interactive element are visually and programmatically available.

provisions.title: Changes To Elements Notified
provisions.text: Changes to interactive element names, roles, values, or states are visually and programmatically indicated.

name: Status Messages
summary: In content built with markup languages, status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties, so assistive technologies can present them without them receiving focus. WCAG defines a status message as a change in content that isn't a change of context and that tells the user about success or results, waiting, progress, or errors.
whyItMatters: Over-announcing (live regions for every update) can drown out the messages that matter.

provisions.title: Change Of Content Notified
provisions.text: Meaningful changes in visual content are conveyed programmatically.
exceptWhen: • changes are continuous, without pause.

name: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded audio in synchronized media has sign language interpretation.
whyItMatters: A small or low-resolution interpreter window makes hand shapes and facial expressions hard to read.

provisions.title: Sign language available (prerecorded)
provisions.text: Sign language interpretation is provided for all prerecorded audio content in the primary sign language that is most appropriate for each intended audience or region.
exceptWhen:
• The audio content is an alternative for visual content and is clearly labeled as such.
  • The audio content is decorative background sound.
  • The audio is an interface sound effect.

related.title: Sign Language Controllable
related.text: A mechanism is available to show and hide sign language interpretation.
exceptWhen:
• Sign language interpretation is hard-coded into the video content.
  • A sign language interpreted version is provided as a separate video.

name: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
summary: Where pauses in the foreground audio are too short for audio description to convey the sense of the video, extended audio description is provided: the video pauses so there is time for more description. Applies to prerecorded video in synchronized media.
whyItMatters: Frequent pauses can make the experience choppy if the description is longer than it needs to be.

provisions.title: Extended Audio Descriptions Available
provisions.text: The video pauses to extend the audio track and provides an extended audio description to describe visual information needed to understand the media.

provisions.title: Extended Audio Descriptions Equivalent
provisions.text: The information conveyed by extended audio descriptions is equivalent to the visual content needed to understand the media.

name: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
summary: All prerecorded synchronized media and all prerecorded video-only media have an alternative for time-based media: a document with correctly sequenced text descriptions of the visual and auditory information, and a way to achieve the outcome of any interaction.
whyItMatters: A complete alternative is little use if users can't find it.

provisions.title: Descriptive Transcripts Available
provisions.text: Descriptive transcripts are provided for prerecorded audio and video content.
exceptWhen:
• The media is purely decorative.
  • The media is already a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
  • The visual track includes no information that is not already conveyed in the audio track (for example, a “talking head” video where only the speaker is visible against a static background).

provisions.title: Transcripts equivalent (prerecorded)
provisions.text: Equivalent transcripts are available for audio and video content.
exceptWhen: • The audio or video has no spoken content and serves only as background.

provisions.title: Visual Information Identified In Transcripts
provisions.text: Visual information needed to understand the media is described in transcripts.

name: Contrast (Enhanced)
summary: Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 7:1, and large-scale text at least 4.5:1, with the same exceptions as 1.4.3.
whyItMatters: Some readers find very high contrast uncomfortable, so a single fixed palette can't suit everyone.

provisions.title: Text contrast sufficient (enhanced)
provisions.text: The default visual presentation of text meets @@[contrast measure to be determined, at a higher level than the core requirement for Text contrast sufficient (minimum)].
exceptWhen:
• the text is:
    • also present elsewhere in the page/view which meets the requirement
    • part of an inactive interactive element
    • pure decoration
    • not visible to anyone
    • part of a picture that includes significant other visual content
    • part of a logo

changeAnalysis.note: The draft's contrast measure is still to be determined.

name: Low or No Background Audio
summary: For prerecorded audio-only content that is mainly foreground speech (not an audio CAPTCHA, audio logo, or singing or rapping), one of these is true: there are no background sounds, they can be turned off, or they are at least 20 decibels quieter than the speech, apart from occasional sounds of one or two seconds.
whyItMatters: Even background music at 20dB lower can make speech hard to follow for people with hearing loss.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers background audio levels.

name: Visual Presentation
summary: For blocks of text, a mechanism is available to: choose foreground and background colors; limit width to 80 characters (40 for CJK); avoid justified text; get line spacing of at least 1.5 and paragraph spacing at least 1.5 times the line spacing; and resize text to 200 percent without horizontal scrolling in a full-screen window.
whyItMatters: Relying on users to find browser settings means many never benefit.

provisions.title: Blocks Of Text Adjustable
provisions.text: The presentation of blocks of text can be adjusted, without loss of content or functionality, to meet the @@ [values to be determined] for: * inline margin * block margin * line length * line height * justification
exceptWhen: • the style attribute is hard-coded, such as raw text that is capitalized or hyphenated.

provisions.title: Blocks of text readable (minimum)
provisions.text: The default/authored presentation of blocks of text meets the minimum @@ [values to be determined] for: * inline margin * block margin * line length * line height

provisions.title: Text Color Adjustable
provisions.text: The foreground and background color of text can be adjusted without losing content or functionality.
exceptWhen:
• the text is:
    • also present elsewhere in the page/view which meets the requirement
    • part of an inactive interactive element
    • pure decoration
    • not visible to anyone
    • part of a picture that includes significant other visual content
    • part of a logo

name: Images of Text (No Exception)
summary: Images of text are used only for pure decoration, or where a particular presentation of text is essential.
whyItMatters: None beyond 1.4.5. This removes 1.4.5's customization exception.

related.title: Text Detectable
related.text: All visible text has a programmatically determinable equivalent.
exceptWhen: • making visible text programmatically determinable would lead to duplication within the view.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft restricts images of text.

name: Keyboard (No Exception)
summary: All functionality can be operated through a keyboard interface without needing specific timing for individual keystrokes. Unlike 2.1.1, there is no exception for path-dependent input.
whyItMatters: Keyboard alternatives for drawing or gesture tools can be technically present but tedious.

provisions.title: Keyboard Operable
provisions.text: All components on the page/view that can be operated by pointer, audio (voice or other), gesture, camera, or other means can be operated using keyboard interface only.

provisions.title: Keyboard Accessible
provisions.text: All content that can be accessed by other input modalities can be accessed using keyboard interface only.

name: No Timing
summary: Timing is not an essential part of the event or activity, except for non-interactive synchronized media and real-time events.
whyItMatters: Removing time limits can conflict with security policies, which need a design answer rather than an exception.

provisions.title: No Time Limits
provisions.text: The completion of a process does not include time limits.
exceptWhen: • the time limit is essential.

name: Interruptions
summary: The user can postpone or suppress interruptions, except interruptions involving an emergency.
whyItMatters: Notification settings buried in account preferences are rarely discovered.

provisions.title: Notifications Adjustable
provisions.text: The timing or positioning of notifications can be changed, suppressed, or saved.
exceptWhen: • The notification involves an emergency or is essential.

name: Three Flashes
summary: Nothing on the page flashes more than three times in any one second. Unlike 2.3.1, there is no threshold exception for small or dim flashes.
whyItMatters: None beyond 2.3.1.

provisions.title: No flashing over threshold (no exceptions)
provisions.text: Flashes are below the general flash and red flash thresholds without a minimum size.

name: Location
summary: Information about the user's location within a set of pages is available.
whyItMatters: Breadcrumbs that only reflect the URL structure may not match how users think about the site.

related.title: Current Step Indicated
related.text: The current step within a multi-step process is visually and programmatically indicated.

related.title: All Steps Listed
related.text: A list of all steps in a multi-step process is visually and programmatically available at each step.
exceptWhen: • The total number of steps is unknown, or the sequence of steps depends on user actions.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers location within a set of pages.

name: Link Purpose (Link Only)
summary: A mechanism is available so that the purpose of each link can be identified from the link text alone, except where the purpose would be ambiguous to everyone.
whyItMatters: Visually hidden text added to make links unique can mismatch what speech-input users see and say.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers link purpose.

name: Section Headings
summary: Section headings are used to organize the content.
whyItMatters: Headings used for styling rather than structure create a misleading outline.

provisions.title: Heading Structure Available
provisions.text: Meaningful blocks of content are organized with a logical hierarchy of headings.
exceptWhen: • The technology does not support heading levels.

name: Target Size (Enhanced)
summary: Pointer targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels. Exceptions: an equivalent target of that size is on the same page; the target is in a sentence or block of text; the browser sets the size and the author hasn't changed it; or the presentation is essential.
whyItMatters: None beyond 2.5.8. This is the stricter version.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers target size.

name: Unusual Words
summary: A mechanism is available for identifying specific definitions of words or phrases used in an unusual or restricted way, including idioms and jargon.
whyItMatters: A glossary on a separate page technically counts but interrupts reading.

provisions.title: Non-literal language explained
provisions.text: Explanations or unambiguous alternatives are available in text content for non-literal language, such as idioms and metaphors.
exceptWhen:
• text content is:
    • poetic,
    • scriptural,
    • artistic, or
    • expressive rather than informational.

provisions.title: Common Words Used
provisions.text: Common words are used, and definitions are available for uncommon words.
exceptWhen:
• the words are for names of people or places, or
  • the language does not have a high-frequency corpus.

name: Abbreviations
summary: A mechanism is available for identifying the expanded form or meaning of abbreviations.
whyItMatters: The abbr title attribute alone isn't reliably exposed to keyboard, touch or screen reader users.

provisions.title: Abbreviations Explained
provisions.text: Explanations of abbreviations are available when first used.
exceptWhen:
• the abbreviation is:
    • used so often it has become a word with its own dictionary entry, such as “scuba,” “info,” and “HTML”,
    • used in a logo, or
    • included in a longer phrase, such as “brand DNA,” whose meaning needs to be defined to meet the non-literal language requirement.

name: Reading Level
summary: When text needs reading ability above lower secondary education level (after removing proper names and titles), supplemental content or a simpler version is available.
whyItMatters: Readability formulas measure sentence and word length, not whether people actually understand the text.

related.title: Summaries Available
related.text: A summary is available for long-form text content and: * is identifiable visually and programmatically, * uses concise sentences, and * provides access to explanations of any uncommon words that are used in the summary.
exceptWhen: • long-form text content continues on multiple pages/views, only the first page/view requires a summary.

related.title: Common Words Used
related.text: Common words are used, and definitions are available for uncommon words.
exceptWhen:
• the words are for names of people or places, or
  • the language does not have a high-frequency corpus.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft uses a reading-level test.

name: Change on Request
summary: Changes of context happen only at the user's request, or there's a mechanism to turn such changes off.
whyItMatters: Opening new windows or tabs without warning remains common and disorienting.

related.title: Focus user-controlled
related.text: The keyboard focus only moves as a result of user interaction.
exceptWhen:
• The keyboard focus automatically moves to the next interactive elements in keyboard navigation order on completion of some user action, such when the focus moves between the fields for a time-based one-time password (TOTP) code.
  • The keyboard focus results from security or emergency situations, such as warning about an imminent session timeout that would cause the user to lose their work.
  • The user is informed of the potential keyboard focus move before it happens and given the chance to avoid the move.

related.title: Change Of User Agent Notified
related.text: When content triggers a device change or an automatic user agent change, the user is notified before the change occurs.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft restricts changes of context to user request.

name: Help
summary: Context-sensitive help is available: help text related to the function currently being performed. A general help page doesn't meet the definition.
whyItMatters: Help that is technically context-sensitive but terse can still leave users stuck.

provisions.title: Contextual Help Available
provisions.text: Context-sensitive help is available.

name: Error Prevention (All)
summary: For pages that require the user to submit information, at least one is true: submissions are reversible; input is checked and the user can correct it; or the user can review, confirm and correct before final submission.
whyItMatters: None beyond 3.3.4. This extends it to every submission.

provisions.title: Errors Preventable
provisions.text: Data entry interfaces allow for users to do at least one of the following before submission: * Review, confirm, and correct all information. * Review and correct input errors found during validation.
exceptWhen: • entered data is auto-saved and/or reversible.

name: Audio-only (Live)
summary: Live audio-only content, such as a live audio stream, has an alternative that presents equivalent information.
whyItMatters: A text summary posted afterwards doesn't help people following the event live.

provisions.title: Dialogue transcripts available (live)
provisions.text: Dialogue transcripts are available for all live audio and video content.
exceptWhen:
• The audio or video content is an alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
  • The audio or video has no spoken content and serves only as background.

name: Identify Purpose
summary: In content built with markup languages, the purpose of user interface components, icons and regions can be programmatically determined.
whyItMatters: Tools that personalize interfaces for people with cognitive disabilities depend on semantics that most sites don't yet provide.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft requires identifying the purpose of components, icons and regions.

name: Re-authenticating
summary: When an authenticated session expires, the user can continue the activity without losing data after signing in again.
whyItMatters: Re-authentication that drops the user on a home page technically keeps their data but loses their place.

related.title: Progress Saved
related.text: Data entry and other task completion processes allow saving and resuming from the current step in the task.
exceptWhen: • The task completion is part of a real-time event, and no alternative to the time limit is possible.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers re-authentication.

name: Timeouts
summary: Users are warned how long they can be inactive before data is lost, unless the data is kept for more than 20 hours of inactivity.
whyItMatters: A warning shown once at the start of a long form is forgotten by the time it matters.

related.title: Time Limits Conveyed
related.text: Users are informed at the start of the process or session that a time limit exists, its length, and that it can be adjusted.
exceptWhen: • hiding the existence of the time limit is essential.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers warnings about inactivity timeouts.

name: Animation from Interactions
summary: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential to the functionality or the information conveyed.
whyItMatters: A site-level toggle that users must find before they feel ill doesn't help on first visit.

related.title: User Settings Supported
related.text: Content responds to users’ platform and user agent accessibility-related settings.

related.title: No Visual Motion
related.text: Content does not include pseudo-motion or visual motion lasting longer than 5 seconds.
exceptWhen: • The motion or pseudo-motion is essential.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft is specific to animation triggered by interaction.

name: Multiple Ways
summary: There is more than one way to find a page within a set of pages, except pages that are the result of, or a step in, a process.
whyItMatters: Two ways that both depend on a complex mega-menu don't really give users a choice.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft requires more than one way to find a page.

name: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
summary: When a component receives keyboard focus, no part of it is hidden by content the author created.
whyItMatters: None beyond 2.4.11. This is the full version.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers focus being obscured.

name: Focus Appearance
summary: When the focus indicator is visible, an area of it is at least as large as a 2 CSS pixel thick perimeter of the unfocused component, and has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 between the same pixels in the focused and unfocused states. It doesn't apply if the browser sets the indicator and the author can't adjust it, or if the author hasn't modified the indicator or its background.
whyItMatters: An indicator can meet the area and contrast numbers yet be hard to spot if it is inside the component or similar to other states such as hover.

provisions.title: Focus Indicator Contrast Sufficient
provisions.text: If a custom focus indicator is used, it has sufficient adjacent contrast and change of contrast.

provisions.title: Focus Indicator Size Sufficient
provisions.text: If a custom focus indicator is used, it has sufficient size and adjacency.

changeAnalysis.note: The draft says "sufficient" without giving numbers.

name: Pointer Gestures
summary: Functionality that uses multipoint gestures (such as pinch) or path-based gestures (such as a swipe pattern) can also be operated with a single pointer without a path-based gesture, unless the gesture is essential.
whyItMatters: A single-pointer alternative hidden in a menu technically passes but is rarely discovered.

provisions.title: Path-based gesture not relied on
provisions.text: Path-based gestures are not the only way of achieving any functionality.
exceptWhen: • A path-based gesture is essential to the functionality.

provisions.title: Simple Pointer Input Available
provisions.text: All functionality and content available using complex pointer inputs is also available using a simple pointer input, or a sequence of simple pointer inputs that do not require timing.

name: Pointer Cancellation
summary: For single-pointer functionality, at least one is true: nothing happens on the down-event; the function completes on the up-event and can be aborted before or undone after; the up-event reverses whatever the down-event did; or completing on the down-event is essential.
whyItMatters: Undo that is only available briefly in a toast is easy to miss for screen reader and magnifier users.

provisions.title: Pointer Activation Controllable
provisions.text: At least one of the following is true for functionality that can be activated using a simple pointer input: No down event : The down event of the pointer is not used to execute any part of the function. Cancel or undo : Completion of the function is on the up event and a mechanism is available to cancel the function before completion, or there is a mechanism to undo the function after completion. Up reversal : The up event reverses any outcome of the preceding down event.
exceptWhen: • Completing the function on the down event is essential.

related.title: Consistent Pointer Cancellation
related.text: The method of pointer cancellation is consistent for each type of interaction within a set of pages/views.
exceptWhen: • It is essential to be different.

name: Motion Actuation
summary: Functionality operated by device motion (such as shaking or tilting) or user motion can also be operated through interface components, and responding to motion can be turned off. Exceptions: the motion works through an accessibility-supported interface, or it's essential and doing it another way would invalidate the activity.
whyItMatters: A motion setting that is off only once the user finds it means people with tremors may trigger actions by accident on first use.

provisions.title: Body Movements Not Relied On
provisions.text: Functionality does not rely solely on full or gross body movement.
exceptWhen: • Full or gross body movement is essential to the functionality.

name: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
summary: Content doesn't restrict the input methods available on a platform, except where that is essential, needed for security, or needed to respect user settings.
whyItMatters: Switching off touch on "desktop" layouts strands people who use a touchscreen with a keyboard.

provisions.title: Input Method Flexible
provisions.text: The ability to switch between input methods is available at any time.

name: Pronunciation
summary: A mechanism is available for identifying the pronunciation of words whose meaning, in context, is ambiguous without knowing how they're pronounced.
whyItMatters: This rarely comes up in English but matters in languages like Japanese and Hebrew.

related.title: Diacritics Available
related.text: Diacritics required to identify the correct meaning of each word are available.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft covers pronunciation.

name: Consistent Navigation
summary: Navigation that is repeated on multiple pages within a set of pages appears in the same relative order each time, unless the user changes it.
whyItMatters: The same order in a different place on the screen still makes users hunt for it.

provisions.title: Consistent Navigation Order
provisions.text: The relative order of navigation items is consistent within blocks of navigation that are repeated on multiple pages/views of the conformance scope or process.

related.title: Consistent Navigation Labels
related.text: The labeling of navigation items within blocks of navigation that are repeated on multiple pages/views in the conformance scope or process is consistent.
exceptWhen: • Labels for navigation items that are marked as ‘current’ within the conformance scope or process.

name: Consistent Identification
summary: Components with the same functionality within a set of pages are identified consistently.
whyItMatters: Consistent labels with inconsistent icons, or the reverse, still undermine recognition.

related.title: Consistent Navigation Labels
related.text: The labeling of navigation items within blocks of navigation that are repeated on multiple pages/views in the conformance scope or process is consistent.
exceptWhen: • Labels for navigation items that are marked as ‘current’ within the conformance scope or process.

related.title: Consistent Control Location
related.text: Where an interactive element with the same purpose is used across pages/views, its visual position in the layout is maintained.
exceptWhen:
• The location changes due to a page variation or viewport change, or
  • The layout changes due to being part of a process.

changeAnalysis.note: No provision in the current draft requires consistent identification of all same-function components.

name: Error Suggestion
summary: If an input error is automatically detected and suggestions for correcting it are known, the suggestions are provided, unless that would compromise the security or purpose of the content.
whyItMatters: Correct suggestions can still be hard to act on, for example when they appear only in a summary at the top of a long form.

provisions.title: Error Suggestions Provided
provisions.text: Error messages include suggestions for corrections.
exceptWhen: • including suggestions would jeopardize the security or purpose of the content.

name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
summary: For pages that create legal commitments or financial transactions, modify or delete user-controllable data, or submit test responses, at least one is true: submissions are reversible; input is checked for errors and the user can correct them; or the user can review, confirm and correct before final submission.
whyItMatters: A review step that users can click through without noticing errors technically confirms, but doesn't prevent costly mistakes.

provisions.title: Errors Preventable
provisions.text: Data entry interfaces allow for users to do at least one of the following before submission: * Review, confirm, and correct all information. * Review and correct input errors found during validation.
exceptWhen: • entered data is auto-saved and/or reversible.

related.title: Consequences Explained Before Agreement
related.text: Legal, financial, privacy, and security consequences are provided before finalizing an agreement.

name: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
summary: No step of an authentication process requires a cognitive function test, unless that step offers another method that doesn't rely on one, or a mechanism to help complete it. Unlike 3.3.8, there are no object-recognition or personal-content exceptions.
whyItMatters: None beyond 3.3.8. This removes 3.3.8's object-recognition and personal-content exceptions.

provisions.title: Cognitive Test Alternatives Available
provisions.text: Processes can be completed without a cognitive function test.

name: Parsing
summary: Nothing. WCAG 2.2 marks this criterion obsolete and removed, so it can't be failed under 2.2. WCAG 2.2's introduction notes that organizations required by policy to conform to WCAG 2.0 or 2.1 may still need to test and report it.
whyItMatters: Invalid markup that doesn't affect the accessibility tree isn't a WCAG failure, but it can make behavior inconsistent across browsers and assistive technologies.

changeAnalysis.note: Obsolete and removed in WCAG 2.2.
